title: Drift Detector report (drift.json)
description: The canonical machine-readable output of a Drift Detector scan. drift.md and dashboard.html are verified projections of this document; drift-scan verify checks that they agree. Structural conformance is checked here; the SEMANTIC invariants (a tile count equals the rows it summarizes, no two findings render identically) live in agent/lib/verify.py, because JSON Schema cannot express them.

schemaVersion.description: The contract this document conforms to. A breaking change bumps this.

generated.description: The scan date (YYYY-MM-DD), passed in as `now` — never wall-clock, so output stays deterministic.

counts.description: Summary tallies. Each is DERIVED from the arrays below and must equal them — that equality is enforced by verify.py, not by this schema.

unaudited.description: Vendors called but whose retirement list is unchecked (UNAUDITED or STALE).

secrets.description: Hardcoded credentials found in a repo's git history (one per leak site, not per gitleaks rule). A 0 here means gitleaks ran and found nothing; a failed run is reported in coverage.secretsErrors, never as a 0.

unscannable.description: Sources requested but unreadable (404/no-access URL, typo, folder with no code). Equals rootsUnscannable length; 'cannot see' is not 'clean'.

actions.description: One remediation job per (repo, and — for a sunset — the retiring operation/path). NOT one per finding: 30 CVEs against a package are one upgrade.

unit.description: For a sunset, the exact thing retiring — operation, apiPath, host, or version. This is what keeps twelve dead calls from collapsing into one row.

refKind.description: For an eol action, whether the ref is a runtime (DevOps) or a framework (Developer). null for cve/sunset.

owner.description: The delivery stream that fixes this. DERIVED from (kind, refKind) and re-checked by verify: cve + runtime-eol = devops; sunset + framework-eol = developer.

status.description: DEPRECATED = the deadline has passed (action required); REVIEW = dated but not yet due, or unscored; EXPOSED = a live leaked credential, which has no deadline because it passed the moment the value was committed.

href.description: A pinned blob permalink, or null when the source host is unknown.

file_count.description: Total distinct call-sites for this action. `files` is a sample capped for display; this is the true count.

catalog.description: Per-vendor catalog-coverage verdicts — whether anyone has checked this vendor's retirement list. A vendor with call-sites and no attestation is UNAUDITED, which is why '0 findings' is not the same as 'clean'. BLOCKED means the check was made and REFUSED — the vendor publishes retirements only behind a partner/seller login — a documented blind spot rather than an unworked one; its call-sites still count as unchecked.

coverageGrades.description: Per-repo shape coverage — whether the scan could read the repo's calls at all.

rootsUnscannable.description: Sources requested but unreadable, carried from inventory coverage so every projection surfaces them and verify enforces it. 'Cannot see' is never 'clean'.

root.description: The requested source (URL or path) that could not be read.

reason.description: Why it could not be read, in the operator's terms.

endpoints.description: Every outbound call the engine read, triaged by hostClass (agent/lib/host_class.py) and coverage lifecycle (agent/lib/dashboard_render.py) — not just catalogued vendors. Deliberately loosely typed below (properties only, none required) rather than not typed at all, matching the rest of this array's actual shape.

classified.description: True for a catalogued vendor — always hostClass 'api'.

ownInfraReason.description: Present only when hostClass is 'own-infra': WHY the host was claimed as this repo's OWN infrastructure, naming the exact signal and the matched value (agent/lib/own_infra.py). Two possible signals, deliberately different weight: a repo-name TOKEN guess (e.g. "repo token 'zenithapp'") is a heuristic, not certain, so the endpoint's coverage stays 'queued' — it can still surface as a real third party through drift-scan research. A git-remote-org DOMAIN claim (e.g. "git remote org domain 'devhost.io'") is the organisation's own identity, strong enough that coverage becomes 'na' — dropped from the research backlog. Absent when no signal claims the host, including when the unrelated multi-host own-infra heuristic (endpoints.py's _tag_own_infra) retagged it instead — that path carries no reason at all.

delta.description: Findings movement since the PREVIOUS scan. `comparedAgainst` is the date of that scan, or null when no baseline existed — a first run reports every finding as `new`, and rendering that as a week's change reads as a catastrophe rather than a first measurement. Same rule as catalogDelta. The rest of the shape (new/resolved/persisting/mutedCount) is deliberately not pinned here; it never was.

catalogSummary.description: The absorption scoreboard: how many DETECTED vendors have had their retirement list checked, and how many have not. The unit is an attestation (somebody opened the vendor's page on a stated date), never an entry count, which is gameable. INTERNAL and ACCEPTED are human-signed terminal dispositions; only INTERNAL settles a vendor, because in-house code has no external lifecycle. ACCEPTED names a risk without measuring it, so its call-sites keep counting toward unauditedCallSites exactly as BLOCKED's do.

internal.description: Vendors signed off as built in-house by a named approver.

accepted.description: Vendors whose residual risk a named approver accepted; still counted as unchecked exposure.

unauditedCallSites.description: Call-sites belonging to vendors nobody has checked a retirement list for. The number that matters: it is the size of the blind spot.

catalogDelta.description: Movement in catalog coverage since the PREVIOUS scan. `comparedAgainst` is the date of that scan, or null when no baseline existed — an empty delta with a null baseline means 'nothing to compare against', NOT 'a quiet week', and must never be rendered as calm.

newlyAttested.description: Vendors already known last scan that have since become CURRENT or INTERNAL. A vendor seen for the first time is NOT listed here — nobody did that work this period.
